the study of formulation factors that could affect the transscleral transport of a 40-kDa dextran.
the study of the iontophoresis parameters and their effect on the permeability of the sclera, and on the post-iontophoresis transscleral transport.

the optimization of iontophoretically enhanced transscleral permeation of high molecular weight hydrophobic drugs, such as peptides and proteins, and with the development of new formulations for the iontophoretical administration of these drugs.

transscleral electroosmotic iontophoresis could be a valid approach for the delivery of high molecular weight drugs, although a careful choice of formulation parameters is required.

the iontophoresis technique can be considered a promising strategy to improve the permeation of neutral high molecular weight drugs across the eye, but the optimization of formulation factors and current intensity is mandatory in order to obtain the best results.

iontophoresis could be a promising technique to promote the trans-sclera transport of high molecular weight hydrophiles.
trans-scleral FD-40 iontophoresis could be a promising technique for the ocular delivery of neutral hydrophilic drugs, although the formulation parameters should be carefully selected.

The main takeaway from our work is that

transscleral and post-iontophoresis transport of high molecular weight compounds could be enhanced by iontophoresis and that this technique could be a valid alternative for the treatment of retinal diseases.

iontophoresis can be a promising approach for the transscleral delivery of neutral high molecular weight compounds, such as growth factors and other proteins, and can be a valid tool to improve the delivery of other compounds to the eye.

iontophoresis, in combination with a proper formulation, could be used to promote the delivery of high molecular weight drugs to the retina, overcoming the main limitation of the ocular route, the low bioavailability.
